content:
**Visual observations:**
- Corn ear exposed with husks peeled back/bleached to a white/pale color
- White fungal growth visible at the base of the ear and on the husk surfaces
- Surrounding plant tissue (leaves, husks) severely dead, gray-brown, dried and shredded
- Kernels visible at the tip appear cream/tan colored and relatively intact
- The bleached husk contrasts with the otherwise dead gray plant material

**Reasoning through candidates:**

- **Ear_rots_Diplodia**: Key features match — white mold starting at the base of the ear, bleached husks, rest of plant dead/gray. The white mycelium growing from the ear base is diagnostic.
- **Ear_rots_Gibberella**: Would show pinkish-red mold at the tip, coming from the silk channel — not present here.
- **Fusarium**: White to pink/salmon cottony mold on scattered/clustered kernels with starburst pattern — the pattern here is more diffuse/basal, not the starburst on individual kernels.
- **Ear_rots_Aspergillus**: Would show olive-green to gray-green powdery mold — not visible here.

The bleached husks combined with white mold at the ear base is the hallmark of Diplodia ear rot. The extensive plant death around the ear is consistent with a severe, late-season infection.
